question: Why does the resistivity of a semiconductor (like Silicon) decrease significantly with rising temperature, contrary to the behavior seen in metals?

options.A: The relaxation time ($\tau$) increases significantly with temperature.
options.B: The number density of charge carriers ($n$) increases exponentially, outweighing the decrease in relaxation time.
options.C: The electrons lose their kinetic energy and move slower.
options.D: The lattice vibrations cease at higher temperatures in semiconductors.
